accepted.question: State the goals of access control and explain the role of a reference monitor in authorization, then describe how the Chinese Wall policy's simple security rule and its write rule constrain an analyst's access.

marking_points.point: Access control has four goals: granting, limiting, preventing and revoking access.
marking_points.quote: Goals of access control: Granting access Limiting access Preventing access Revoking access

marking_points.point: A reference monitor is the component that makes authorization decisions.
marking_points.quote: Reference monitor makes authorization decisions.

marking_points.point: Reference monitors are the instruments used to realize access control policies and can be deployed at every level of the system hierarchy.
marking_points.quote: Reference monitors are instruments for realization of access control policies. They can be deployed at all levels of system hierarchy.

marking_points.point: Under the simple security rule, a subject may access information from any company provided it has never accessed information from a different company in the same conflict class.
marking_points.quote: A subject may access information from any company as long as that subject has never accessed information from a different company in the same conflict class.

marking_points.point: Under the write rule, write access is allowed only if the simple security rule permits it and no object readable by the subject lies in a different company dataset and holds unsanitized information.
marking_points.quote: (Chinese Wall) *-property: Write access is only permitted if: access is permitted by the simple security rule, and no object can be read which is: in a different company dataset than the one for which write access is requested, and contains unsanitized information.

questions.question: Describe six facts about Kerberos and single sign-on mechanisms, covering their motivation, design criteria, login procedure and role in distributed environments.

marking_points.point: Single sign-on reduces the need for users to memorize passwords.
marking_points.quote: Reduce the need to memorize passwords

marking_points.point: Single sign-on reduces the time users spend typing passwords.
marking_points.quote: Reduce the time spent on typing passwords

marking_points.point: Kerberos is designed to be secure against eavesdropping by never transmitting passwords in clear text.
marking_points.quote: Security against eavesdropping: no                                       password transmission in clear text.

marking_points.point: Kerberos is designed for transparency, so the user is unaware of any authentication beyond the initial login.
marking_points.quote: Transparency: user is not aware of any                            authentication beyond an initial login.

marking_points.point: During Kerberos login, the hash of the user's password becomes the secret key of the client/user.
marking_points.quote: The hash value of his password                                                      KU = h(P) becomes a secret key of the                                                  client/user.

marking_points.point: Single sign-on methods such as Kerberos automate authentication in large distributed environments.
marking_points.quote: Single sign-on methods such as Kerberos provide means for automating authentication in large distributed environments.

questions.question: State six facts about biometric mechanisms and technologies, covering the definition of a biometric, the two application sectors, and specific biometric technologies with their characteristics.

marking_points.point: A biometric is defined as a physiological or behavioural characteristic of a human being that can distinguish one person from another and can theoretically be used for identification or verification of identity.
marking_points.quote: A biometric is a physiological or behavioural characteristic of a human being that can distinguish one person from another and that theoretically can be used for identification or verification of identity.

marking_points.point: Biometric applications available today are divided into two sectors: psychological and behavioural.
marking_points.quote: Biometric applications available today are categorized into 2 sectors

marking_points.point: The psychological sector includes iris, fingerprints, hand, retinal and face recognition.
marking_points.quote: Psychological: Iris, Fingerprints, Hand, Retinal and Face recognition

marking_points.point: The behavioural sector includes voice, typing pattern and signature.
marking_points.quote: Behavioural: Voice, Typing pattern, Signature

marking_points.point: Fingerprint processing divides the print into loops, whorls and arch and calculates minutiae points (ridge endings).
marking_points.quote: Divides print into loops, whorls and arch

marking_points.point: Iris scanning reads the unique pattern of the iris, which is coloured and visible from far, and requires no touch, overcoming retinal scanner issues.
marking_points.quote: Scans unique pattern of iris

questions.question: State SIX (6) techniques by which malware propagates itself or infects a host system, as described in the lecture.

marking_points.point: A virus can spread by appending its virus body onto a host program.
marking_points.quote: Append a virus body to a program

marking_points.point: An executable virus can save the original program entry point inside the virus body so control returns after infection.
marking_points.quote: Save an entry point to a program in a virus body

marking_points.point: An EXE infector can overwrite the program header so that the entry point is switched to the virus.
marking_points.quote: Over write a program header to switch the entry point to a virus

marking_points.point: The infected EXE jumps back to the original entry point during execution, hiding the infection from the user.

questions.question: Explain six aspects of the security mechanisms provided by Windows, including how subjects and their credentials are handled, how resources are organised, and why the complexity of these mechanisms can itself be a risk.

marking_points.point: Windows offers elaborate built-in mechanisms covering user accounts, objects and access control.
marking_points.quote: Windows systems contain complex security mechanisms for user account and object management as well as access control.

marking_points.point: Discretionary access control lists allow detailed, fine-grained control over diverse objects both in the OS and in applications.
marking_points.quote: DACS enable ﬁne-grained access control of heterogeneous entities in Windows itself as well as applications.

marking_points.point: The very complexity of these mechanisms is a weakness, since misconfiguration or coding bugs can cause serious security breaches.
marking_points.quote: The complexity of Windows security mechanisms is also its enemy: misconﬁguration as well as implementation bugs may lead to severe security incidents.

marking_points.point: Active Directory, introduced with Windows 2000, acts as an LDAP-style directory for organising system resources.
marking_points.quote: Active directory introduced in Windows 2000 is an LDAP-like directory service for organization of system resources:

marking_points.point: Processes and threads are the active subjects in Windows, and their security credentials are kept in a token.
marking_points.quote: Windows subjects are processes and threads.

marking_points.point: Tokens are passed down to newly created processes, possibly with restrictions applied.
marking_points.quote: Tokens are inherited (possibly with restrictions) during creation of new processes.

questions.question: Describe the Samy worm attack by stating how the malicious script was injected, how it spread, and its outcome.

marking_points.point: The attacker injected JavaScript into a user profile using document.body.innerHTML.
marking_points.quote: Inject Javascript into a user proﬁle using document.body.innerHTML

marking_points.point: The worm obtained the list of the user's friends (heros) by sending a GET request to a user profile.
marking_points.quote: Get the list of user’s heros by using a GET on a user proﬁle

marking_points.point: It added Samy as a friend by performing XML-HTTP on the addFriends page.
marking_points.quote: Add Samy as a ﬁeld by performing XML-HTTP on the addFriends page

marking_points.point: Any user visiting an infected profile had their own profile and friends list infected, causing further spread.
marking_points.quote: Any user who visits an infected user’s page will gets proﬁle infected with Javascript and his friends list infected with Samy

marking_points.point: The attack ultimately infected about 1,000,000 MySpace profiles.
marking_points.quote: Eventually about 1,000,000 MySpace proﬁles were infected.

marking_points.point: The underlying XSS vulnerability exists because any web application that returns user input without filtering is potentially vulnerable.
marking_points.quote: Any web application that returns user input without ﬁltering is a potential XSS vulnerability!

questions.question: Refer to your answer in (a). Based on the scenario in (a), explain six preventive network security mechanisms that could be deployed alongside the NIDS to protect the organization's network, covering firewalls, proxy servers, segmentation, VPNs, ZTNA and IDS/IPS.

marking_points.point: A firewall controls incoming and outgoing network traffic according to predetermined security policies.
marking_points.quote: Control incoming and outgoing traffic on network with predetermined security policies.

marking_points.point: A proxy server improves data security and network performance by acting as a firewall and web filter, sharing connections and caching data.
marking_points.quote: Proxy servers act as a firewall                                                  and web filter, provide shared network                                             connections, and cache data to speed up                                               common requests.

marking_points.point: Network segmentation places boundaries between segments whose computing assets share a common function, risk or role.
marking_points.quote: Boundaries between network segments where                                    computing assets within the segment have a common                           function, risk or role within an organization.

marking_points.point: A remote access VPN gives individual hosts or clients secure access to the organization's network.
marking_points.quote: Provides remote and secure access to an organization network to individual hosts or clients

marking_points.point: Zero Trust Network Access restricts each user to only the access and permissions required for their role.
marking_points.quote: A user                                              should only has access and permission that                                            required to fulfill the role

marking_points.point: IDS/IPS detect or prevent attacks such as brute force, denial-of-service and exploitation of network vulnerabilities.
